metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with entry point (Lambda handler in src/server.ts), dependency manifest (package.json), and resource-provisioning IaC (infra/template.yaml with AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway). Single deployable service.
metadata.archetype_justification: DynamoDB persistent data store with CRUD operations on product entities (upsert, soft-delete, query). Write endpoints mutate state. No downstream service fan-out.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 2.83 yields Partial band (equivalent to Pilot-Ready) but 3 High findings (INF-Q11, OPS-Q5, OPS-Q6) force Remediation Required tier. The application is well-architected for cloud-native infrastructure (strong INF 3.36, DATA 3.75, SEC 3.00) but has significant operational maturity gaps (OPS 1.22) concentrated in CI/CD, deployment, and testing.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipeline — all deployments are manual
top_gaps.impact: Blocks safe, repeatable deployments and prevents all other DevOps improvements

top_gaps.title: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: No canary or blue/green deployment — direct-to-production
top_gaps.impact: Regressions reach 100% of traffic instantly with no rollback mechanism

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.impact: Cannot verify system behavior end-to-end before deployment

top_gaps.title: Application Security Pipeline
top_gaps.gap: No SAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning
top_gaps.impact: Vulnerabilities in npm dependencies reach production undetected

top_gaps.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting

top_gaps.impact: Failures go undetected until user reports

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming — No event emission on state changes
findings.description: The service is entirely synchronous. Mutations that change product state (upsert, soft-delete) do not emit events for downstream consumers or audit. The README explicitly identifies the missing audit event on deleteProduct.
findings.gap: No event emission on state-changing mutations. For a stateful-crud, state changes should publish events to enable downstream notification and audit.
findings.recommendation: Enable DynamoDB Streams on ProductsTable and publish state-change events via EventBridge or connect a Lambda consumer for audit logging.

findings.title: Network Security — No VPC or network-layer controls
findings.description: Serverless architecture relies on IAM and service-to-service TLS rather than VPC/subnet network segmentation. Lambda accesses DynamoDB via AWS service endpoints without VPC placement.
findings.gap: No VPC endpoints or network-layer controls. Relies entirely on IAM for isolation rather than network segmentation with managed networking services.
findings.recommendation: For this serverless architecture, the current design is acceptable. For additional defense-in-depth, consider adding a VPC with DynamoDB gateway endpoint.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — No restore testing or cross-region replication
findings.description: DynamoDB PITR enabled with 35-day retention. However, no documented restore procedure, no cross-region backup replication, no AWS Backup plan resource.
findings.gap: Missing documented restore procedure, cross-region backup replication, and centralized backup management via AWS Backup.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS::Backup::BackupPlan resource for centralized management and cross-region copy rules. Document and test restore procedure.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — Missing operational resources
findings.description: SAM template covers compute, API, data, auth, and tracing (70-90% coverage). Missing: CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, and operational monitoring resources.
findings.gap: No CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, or Route 53 health checks defined in IaC. Monitoring and alerting are not codified.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda errors, DynamoDB throttle events, and API Gateway 5xx rates. Add a CloudWatch dashboard for the service.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline definitions found. No .github/workflows/, no buildspec.yml, no Jenkinsfile, no CodePipeline definitions. All deployments are manual.
findings.gap: Complete absence of CI/CD automation. Application code and infrastructure changes are deployed manually with no automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with build (tsc), test (vitest run), and deploy (sam deploy) stages. GitHub Actions or AWS CodePipeline + CodeBuild are suitable.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — Entirely synchronous with no event emission
findings.description: All communication is synchronous GraphQL request/response. No event emission on state changes. README identifies missing audit event on deleteProduct as known gap.
findings.gap: For a stateful-crud, state-changing operations should emit events for downstream consumers and audit. No async communication patterns exist.
findings.recommendation: Enable DynamoDB Streams or add EventBridge PutEvents on mutations to emit state-change events for audit logging and downstream integration.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — No versioning exists
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. GraphQL endpoint at /graphql with no version prefix. No @deprecated directives in schema. No documented backward-compatibility policy.
findings.gap: Breaking schema changes would affect all consumers simultaneously with no migration path or deprecation period.
findings.recommendation: Implement GraphQL deprecation strategy: use @deprecated directives on fields before removal, document schema evolution policy, consider field-level sunset dates.

findings.title: Service Discovery — Environment variables only
findings.description: Service uses environment variables for resource discovery (TABLE env var via CloudFormation !Ref). API Gateway endpoint discoverable via stack outputs. No dynamic service registry or API catalog.
findings.gap: No dynamic service discovery. Downstream consumers must know the API Gateway URL through manual configuration or stack output lookups.
findings.recommendation: Register the GraphQL endpoint in AWS Cloud Map or publish to an API catalog for automated discovery.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — No S3 infrastructure
findings.description: Service stores structured product data exclusively in DynamoDB. No unstructured data (documents, images, files) is handled. No S3 buckets or document parsing infrastructure.
findings.gap: No S3 infrastructure for unstructured data if the catalog evolves to include product images or rich media.
findings.recommendation: If product images or rich media are planned, add S3 bucket infrastructure. For current structured-data-only scope, this is a minor forward-looking gap.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — AWS-managed encryption only
findings.description: DynamoDB table has SSE enabled with AWS-managed encryption (AWS-owned key). All data at rest is encrypted but using AWS-managed rather than customer-managed KMS keys.
findings.gap: Uses AWS-managed encryption rather than customer-managed KMS keys. No explicit key rotation policy or customer control over encryption key lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: For sensitive data, upgrade to customer-managed KMS key. For a product catalog with no PII, AWS-managed encryption may be acceptable.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — No dependency vulnerability scanning
findings.description: Lambda runtime auto-patched by AWS. However, no application dependency vulnerability scanning — no Dependabot, Renovate, npm audit, or Snyk configured.
findings.gap: npm dependencies are not monitored for CVEs. Application-level packages could contain known vulnerabilities without detection.
findings.recommendation: Add .github/dependabot.yml or renovate.json for automated dependency updates. Add npm audit as a pre-deployment check.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists for security tools to integrate into.
findings.gap: Complete absence of automated security scanning. Vulnerable dependencies and application security issues reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot or Renovate for dependency scanning. Integrate npm audit --audit-level=high as a pipeline gate once CI/CD is established. Add SAST tool (Semgrep).

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — Gaps at API Gateway layer
findings.description: X-Ray Active tracing enabled on Lambda function, auto-instrumenting AWS SDK calls. API Gateway HTTP API stage does not explicitly enable X-Ray tracing.
findings.gap: Full request path (client → API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB) may have gaps at the API Gateway layer. No custom trace annotations.
findings.recommendation: Add TracingEnabled on HttpApi stage for complete end-to-end tracing. Add custom annotations for business context.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions found. No CloudWatch alarms on latency or error rate. No error budget tracking. No monitoring artifacts.
findings.gap: No formal service level objectives. Cannot measure whether the service meets user expectations or degrading over time.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: p99 latency < 200ms, availability > 99.9%, error rate < 0.1%. Add CloudWatch alarms for these thresholds.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No custom metrics published
findings.description: No custom business metrics. No cloudwatch.put_metric_data calls. Service relies entirely on default Lambda/DynamoDB CloudWatch metrics.
findings.gap: No business outcome metrics — no tracking of product queries, catalog updates, or API usage patterns by consumer.
findings.recommendation: Add custom CloudWatch metrics using Embedded Metric Format: ProductQueried, ProductUpserted, ProductDeleted.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — No alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms. No anomaly detection. No PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. Failures go undetected.
findings.gap: Complete absence of alerting. Lambda errors, DynamoDB throttles, elevated latency, and API Gateway 5xx responses are not monitored.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms: Lambda Errors > 0, Duration p99 > 5000ms, API Gateway 5xxError > 0. Add anomaly detection on error rate.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — Direct-to-production with no staged rollout
findings.description: No deployment strategy configured. SAM function has no DeploymentPreference. Deployments are all-at-once with no canary, linear, or blue/green rollout.
findings.gap: All deployments affect 100% of traffic instantly. No alarm-triggered rollback mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Add DeploymentPreference: { Type: Canary10Percent5Minutes, Alarms: [LambdaErrorAlarm] } to the SAM function for canary deployments with automatic rollback.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No tests exist
findings.description: No test files in repository. vitest configured as dev dependency with test script, but no tests written. No integration, unit, or contract tests.
findings.gap: Complete absence of automated tests. Cannot verify system behavior before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests using vitest against DynamoDB Local. Test happy paths for product, products, upsertProduct, and deleteProduct.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — No runbooks or automation
findings.description: No runbooks, incident response workflows, or self-healing automation found. No SSM documents, no remediation Lambdas.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc. No documented procedures for common failure scenarios.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents: DynamoDB throttling, Lambda concurrency exhaustion, API Gateway rate limiting. Consider SSM Automation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No ownership defined
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS file. No per-service dashboards in IaC. No named alarm owners or team attribution.
findings.gap: No clear ownership of observability assets. No dashboards, no alarms with owner attribution.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch dashboard in IaC. Add CODEOWNERS file. Tag alarms with team ownership.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance — No tags on resources
findings.description: No tags on any resources in the SAM template. Lambda function, DynamoDB table, and API Gateway have no Tags property.
findings.gap: Cannot track costs, identify ownership, or enforce budget controls. No tagging standard.
findings.recommendation: Add tags to all resources: Environment, Service, Owner, CostCenter. Use SAM Globals.Function.Tags for defaults.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: All compute on Lambda (serverless). SAM template defines AWS::Serverless::Function.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB is fully managed with automated failover, PITR, and SSE.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: No multi-step workflows exist in this simple CRUD service. All operations are single-step DynamoDB calls.

evaluations.title: API Entry Point
evaluations.reason: API Gateway HTTP API with Cognito JWT authorizer as managed entry point.

evaluations.title: Auto-Scaling
evaluations.reason: Lambda auto-scales by design. DynamoDB PAY_PER_REQUEST auto-scales capacity.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: Lambda and DynamoDB are inherently multi-AZ. Full stack is fault-tolerant by design.

evaluations.title: Programming Languages
evaluations.reason: Node.js 20+ with TypeScript 5.4, Apollo Server 4, AWS SDK v3. Modern stack.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Well-defined microservice with single responsibility, own data store, clear GraphQL contract.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: No operations exceed 30 seconds. All DynamoDB operations are fast with explicit pagination limits.

evaluations.title: Unified Data Access Layer
evaluations.reason: All DynamoDB access centralized through single DynamoDBDocument client passed via GraphQL context.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB is versionless — AWS manages all versioning transparently. No EOL risk.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: No stored procedures. DynamoDB NoSQL with all business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Application-level IaC only (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB). CloudTrail is an account-level concern belonging in foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: All endpoints protected by Cognito JWT authorizer. Mutations require catalog:write scope.

evaluations.title: Centralized Identity Integration
evaluations.reason: Integrates with Amazon Cognito as centralized IdP. JWT tokens issued by Cognito User Pool.

evaluations.title: Secrets Management
evaluations.reason: No secrets to manage. Lambda uses IAM role for DynamoDB access. No credentials stored.
